title: An EC private key whose lines sit behind a quote, comment or table prefix passes the leak scan
goal: The leak scan flags an EC private key whose armor and body lines carry a Markdown quote, a # or // comment prefix, or share a table row, as it flags a bare PEM block

run:
import base64, os, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
b = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(96)).decode()
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
cases = {"quote": "> " + arm + "\n> " + b[:64] + "\n> " + b[64:], "hash": "# " + arm + "\n# " + b[:64], "slash": "// " + arm + "\n// " + b[:64], "table": "| " + arm + " | " + b[:64] + " |"}
miss = [k for k, v in cases.items() if not hit(v)]
print("prefixed bodies passing:", miss)
sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-tsb23kev focused review of BG-3vnu37rq (reviewer session a419aba4) on origin/main 902e961a9; repro fails there. Premise 2026-10-23 on 35b5b7cb2: the repro exits 1, all four prefixed shapes pass (quote, hash, slash, table).
